hero.title: Built for speed. Designed for growth.
hero.titleLine2: Digital systems and automation that hold up in daily operations.
hero.sub: From resilient Next.js architectures and purpose-built AI integrations to end-to-end process automation. You scale the business — I deliver the technical foundation that carries it.

services.title: Digital, automated, verifiable
services.body: Four areas that belong together: AI, speed, stability and automation — so you can grow without the technology slowing you down.

cards.title: AI adoption & interfaces that stay fast
cards.description: AI assistants integrated where they measurably take load off support and sales. Booking flows and interactive interfaces with short loading times as a binding quality criterion.

cards.title: Technical integrity & system stability
cards.description: Thorough code reviews, targeted defect fixing and preventive speed work. Your systems stay fast, secure and ready for round-the-clock operation.

cards.title: Data engineering & process automation
cards.description: Away from grown Excel solutions towards systems that feed themselves through interfaces. Your business applications talk to each other, and financial reporting is produced without manual intermediate steps.

cards.title: Quantitative analysis & research tooling
cards.description: PineScript indicators and evaluations over historical price data for quantitative market research — from raw data to decisions you can defend.

about.title: Why Kresic Digital Systems?
about.body: I work with an AI-assisted engineering process: AI tooling for implementation, a second AI-assisted pass for review. Before anything ships, every change goes through type checking, static analysis and automated tests all the way to browser interaction. That is how technical debt gets paid down here — documented and traceable rather than merely promised.
about.altText: Danijel Kresic, founder of Kresic Digital Systems
about.figcaptionSub: AI-assisted delivery · every change automatically verified

projects.title: Projects & tooling
projects.intro: My own work in stability, automation and quantitative research — the first two with open source and verifiable checks. What runs here is what I build, in the same form, for your operation.
projects.legalNote: Important note: my work covers quantitative research and educational tooling only — no investment advice, no trading signals and no automated execution.

featured.name: 3D portfolio — Next.js & Three.js
featured.summary: Source code of this website: three-dimensional opening view, current Next.js structure and a setup that allows fast changes.
featured.outcome: An openly readable reference: 3D rendering in the browser, end-to-end typing and delivery over a global edge network — cleared for reuse and extension.

featured.name: Trading Journal — process analytics over a live book
featured.summary: A Next.js journal for a single trader: manual capture of closed positions, process-adherence scoring, limit monitoring for prop accounts and analysis across the whole data set.
featured.outcome: Public under AGPL-3.0. Over 2,300 automated checks run through seven stages on every change; the running application links the exact revision it was built from.

featured.name: Own data pipelines for market analysis
featured.summary: Interface-fed pipelines that turn live price data, fundamentals and market reports (e.g. CFTC Commitment of Traders) into a structured, automated analysis.
featured.outcome: Running in my own operation — built to keep the technique in continuous use, not produced under a client engagement. I set up the same architecture around your data sources and your reporting.

opSec.title: Security & confidentiality
opSec.intro: Fixed rules apply to sensitive engagements: encrypted communication, isolated working environments and contractually binding confidentiality.

items.title: End-to-end encrypted communication
items.body: Project communication and confidential documents run over end-to-end encrypted channels (Proton Mail) as a matter of course — an established procedure, not a case-by-case decision.

items.title: Isolated working environments
items.body: Confidential logic, reports and credentials are processed in a dedicated, isolated environment per engagement — separated from everything else and logged so the work stays auditable.

items.title: NDAs & confidentiality
items.body: On request I sign an NDA before any documents are exchanged. Project details, credentials and proprietary information are kept compartmentalised; access is granted only where a specific task requires it.

items.title: AI tooling with training switched off
items.body: Every AI tool in use runs with training opt-out and privacy mode enabled, so your content does not feed the training of third-party models. What I cannot pass on at this level is a contractual zero-retention guarantee from the providers — where your engagement rules out any transfer to third parties, I work without these tools.

widerruf.htmlBody:
Right of Withdrawal

This is a courtesy translation. The contract and this notice are governed by German law; in case of any discrepancy, the German version is authoritative.

Consumers have a statutory right of withdrawal for contracts concluded by distance communication. A consumer is any natural person who enters into a legal transaction for purposes that are predominantly outside their trade, business, or profession (§ 13 German Civil Code, BGB).

Right of withdrawal

You have the right to withdraw from this contract within fourteen days without giving any reason.

The withdrawal period is fourteen days from the day the contract was concluded.

To exercise your right of withdrawal, you must inform me

Danijel Kresic
Burggasse 3
89604 Allmendingen
Germany
E-mail: kresic.systems@protonmail.com

by means of a clear statement (e.g. a letter sent by post or an e-mail) of your decision to withdraw from this contract. You may use the model withdrawal form set out below, but it is not obligatory.

To meet the withdrawal deadline, it is sufficient for you to send your communication concerning the exercise of the right of withdrawal before the withdrawal period has expired.

Effects of withdrawal

If you withdraw from this contract, I shall reimburse to you all payments received from you without undue delay and in any event not later than fourteen days from the day on which I am informed about your decision to withdraw from this contract. I will carry out such reimbursement using the same means of payment as you used for the initial transaction, unless you have expressly agreed otherwise; in any event, you will not incur any fees as a result of such reimbursement.

If you requested that the services begin during the withdrawal period, you shall pay me an amount which is in proportion to what has been provided until you have communicated to me your withdrawal from this contract, in comparison with the full coverage of the contract.

Early expiry of the right of withdrawal

For a contract for the supply of services, your right of withdrawal expires early once I have fully performed the service, provided that performance began only after you gave your express consent and simultaneously acknowledged that you would lose your right of withdrawal upon complete performance of the contract by me (§ 356(4) BGB).

Model withdrawal form

(If you wish to withdraw from the contract, please complete this form and send it back.)

To
Danijel Kresic
Burggasse 3
89604 Allmendingen
Germany
E-mail: kresic.systems@protonmail.com

I/We (*) hereby give notice that I/We (*) withdraw from my/our (*) contract for the supply of the following service:

  • Description of the service
  • Ordered on
  • Name of consumer(s)
  • Address of consumer(s)
  • Signature of consumer(s) (only if this form is notified on paper)
  • Date

(*) Delete as appropriate.

Note for business customers

The statutory right of withdrawal applies only to consumers within the meaning of § 13 BGB. Contracts with entrepreneurs within the meaning of § 14 BGB carry no statutory right of withdrawal.

General Terms and Conditions

This is a courtesy translation. The contract and these terms are governed by German law; in case of any discrepancy, the German version is authoritative.

These General Terms and Conditions are divided into three parts. Part A applies to all contracts. Part B applies only to consumers. Part C applies only to businesses. Every provision in Parts B and C names who it binds.

Part A — General provisions

Section 1 Scope and definitions

(1) These General Terms and Conditions (the “Terms”) apply to all contracts between Danijel Kresic, Kresic Digital Systems, Burggasse 3, 89604 Allmendingen, Germany (the “Contractor”) and his clients (the “Client”) concerning IT services, software development, web architecture, automation, data processing, quantitative analysis and related services.

(2) A consumer is any natural person who enters into a legal transaction for purposes that are predominantly outside their trade, business or profession (§ 13 German Civil Code, BGB). A business is a natural or legal person or a partnership with legal capacity acting, when concluding the contract, in the exercise of its trade, business or profession (§ 14 BGB).

(3) Part A applies to all contracts. Part B applies only to consumers, Part C only to businesses. Where Part B or Part C departs from Part A, it prevails.

(4) Terms individually agreed between the parties always prevail over these Terms (§ 305b BGB).

(5) The Client’s own general terms do not become part of the contract, even where the Contractor does not expressly object to them in an individual case.

Section 2 Formation of the contract

(1) The presentation of services on the Contractor’s website is not a binding offer but an invitation to enquire.

(2) On request the Contractor prepares an individual offer in text form. Unless stated otherwise in it, the offer is binding for fourteen days from receipt.

(3) The contract is formed when the Client accepts the offer in text form within that period.

(4) These Terms become part of the contract where the Contractor expressly refers to them in the offer and gives the Client a reasonable opportunity to take note of their content; by accepting the offer the Client agrees to their application (§ 305 Abs. 2 BGB).

(5) The Contractor stores the contract text and sends it to the Client together with these Terms in text form. The language of the contract is German.

Section 3 Subject matter and type of contract

(1) The content and scope of the services owed follow exclusively from the offer and the description of services it contains.

(2) The type of contract is expressly named in the offer for each service:

  • Works services are services owing a defined result — for example the creation of a website, a delimited software module or a completed analysis (§ 631 BGB, Werkvertrag).
  • Service contracts are services owing an activity rather than a defined result — for example ongoing support, maintenance, consulting or development billed by time (§ 611 BGB, Dienstvertrag).

(3) The Contractor may render the agreed service by equivalent technical means, provided this is reasonable for the Client and does not impair the purpose assumed under the contract.

(4) The following are not owed: any particular search engine ranking, any particular reach, any particular commercial success, and compatibility with future versions of third-party software not published at the time the contract was formed.

(5) Quantitative analysis services serve research and information purposes only. They constitute neither investment advice nor investment brokerage, neither trading recommendations nor automated order execution.

Section 4 The Client’s duties to cooperate

(1) Performance depends on the Client’s cooperation. The Client shall provide to the Contractor, in good time and free of charge, in particular:

  • a contact person authorised to decide, and a deputy;
  • the necessary access to hosting, domain and DNS, repositories, test accounts and interfaces, in each case over a secure channel;
  • content such as texts, images, logos and data in the agreed formats and by the agreed dates;
  • a test or development environment and suitable test data, where the service requires it;
  • the names of the persons entitled to commission changes of scope under Section 5.

(2) The Client answers queries and grants required approvals within five working days of receipt, unless the offer agrees another period.

(3) If the Client fails to cooperate, or does so late or incompletely, agreed dates and periods are extended by the duration of the delay plus a reasonable restart period.

(4) If the Client is in default with an act of cooperation incumbent on it, the Contractor may, after prior reminder setting a reasonable deadline, claim reasonable compensation for the waiting time (§ 642 BGB). Further statutory claims remain unaffected.

Section 5 Changes of scope

(1) Either party may propose a change to the agreed scope in text form.

(2) The Contractor assesses the proposal within five working days and states in text form what effect the change has on scope, remuneration and dates.

(3) The change takes effect only once both parties have confirmed it in text form.

(4) Until confirmation, work continues on the originally agreed scope. Where the proposed change makes that impossible, the affected dates are extended accordingly.

(5) Services that are not part of the description of services agreed in the offer constitute a change within the meaning of this Section and not a remedy of defects.

Section 6 Dates and deadlines

(1) Dates and deadlines are binding only where the offer or a change agreement expressly designates them as binding. All other indications of time are non-binding estimates.

(2) Compliance with binding dates presupposes that the Client has performed its duties to cooperate under Section 4 in good time.

Section 7 Acceptance of works services

(1) On completion of a works service the Contractor requests acceptance (Abnahme) from the Client in text form and allows a review period of fourteen days.

(2) Acceptance is declared in text form; at either party’s request an acceptance record is drawn up.

(3) The Client may not refuse acceptance on account of immaterial defects. Reservations regarding known defects must be declared on acceptance.

(4) If the Client does not refuse acceptance within the review period stating at least one defect, the works service is deemed accepted (§ 640 Abs. 2 BGB). Section 23 of these Terms applies to consumers.

(5) On acceptance the risk passes to the Client, the remuneration falls due, and the limitation period for claims in respect of defects begins.

(6) If the Client puts the works service into use without having accepted it, this does not replace acceptance; paragraph 4 remains unaffected.

Section 8 Remuneration and payment

(1) The remuneration follows from the offer. It is agreed either as a fixed price for a delimited service or by time on the basis of the agreed hourly rate.

(2) Where billing is by time, the Contractor documents the hours worked in a comprehensible form.

(3) For works services the Contractor may request instalments in the amount of the value of the services actually rendered and owed under the contract (§ 632a BGB). The payment schedule is set out in the offer and follows the actual progress of the work.

(4) Expenses that the Contractor incurs on the Client’s behalf and in the Client’s interest — in particular domain and hosting fees and third-party licences — are charged separately at cost. They are named in the offer to the extent they are foreseeable when the contract is formed.

(5) The Contractor is a small business within the meaning of § 19 UStG. No value added tax is charged and none is shown. All prices stated are final prices.

(6) Invoices are payable in full within fourteen days of receipt.

Section 9 Late payment

(1) If the Client is late in paying, the claim bears interest in accordance with the statutory provisions (§ 288 BGB).

(2) For each further reminder after default has arisen the Contractor may claim the costs actually incurred. The right to claim higher damages for delay is reserved; the Client remains free to prove that the loss was lower.

(3) Where the Client is more than fourteen days late with a payment due, the Contractor may, after prior notice in text form, suspend further performance until payment is made. Dates are extended accordingly.

Section 10 Rights of use

(1) The Contractor grants the Client a non-exclusive right of use, unlimited in time and territory, in the work results for the purpose assumed under the contract. The right of use includes the right to modify and develop the results further and the right to transfer it to a legal successor of the Client’s business.

(2) An exclusive right of use is granted only where expressly agreed in the offer and separately remunerated.

(3) The grant of rights of use is subject to the condition precedent of payment in full of the agreed remuneration. Until then use is permitted revocably only.

(4) The Contractor remains entitled to continue using, without restriction and including for other clients, general knowledge, experience, methods and the generic building blocks, libraries and tools he has developed, provided these contain no confidential information and no individual content of the Client.

(5) Work results regularly contain open-source components and third-party software. In these the Contractor cannot grant rights going beyond the respective third-party licence. The components used and the licence terms applying to them are named to the Client on request. The Client is obliged to comply with those licence terms.

Section 11 Content supplied by the Client

(1) The Client warrants that it holds the necessary rights in all content it supplies — in particular texts, images, graphics, logos, fonts, data and software — and that the use of that content in accordance with the contract infringes no third-party rights.

(2) The Client indemnifies the Contractor against third-party claims asserted against the Contractor on account of the use of supplied content and reimburses the reasonable costs of legal defence. This does not apply where the Contractor is responsible for the infringement.

(3) The Contractor is not obliged to examine supplied content for infringements.

Section 12 Claims in respect of defects

(1) The statutory rights in respect of defects (§§ 633 et seq. BGB) apply to works services, subject to this Section and to Sections 24 and 27.

(2) The Client reports defects in text form and describes them precisely enough for them to be reproduced.

(3) The Contractor first has the right to cure (Nacherfüllung). A reasonable period must be allowed for this. Only after it has expired without success are the Client’s further statutory rights available.

(4) There is no defect where the deviation results from:

  • changes made to the work results by the Client or a third party without the Contractor’s consent;
  • operation outside the system environment described in the offer;
  • content or specifications supplied by the Client;
  • changes to third-party software, interfaces or services after acceptance.

(5) Service contracts are governed by the law of service contracts; as no defined result is owed, no rights in respect of defects arise in that regard.

Section 13 Liability

(1) The Contractor is liable without limitation for damage arising from injury to life, body or health, for intent and gross negligence, for fraudulent concealment of a defect, to the extent of any guarantee given, and under the Product Liability Act.

(2) In cases of simple negligence the Contractor is liable only for breach of a material contractual obligation — an obligation whose fulfilment makes the proper performance of the contract possible in the first place and on whose observance the Client may regularly rely. In that case liability is limited to the foreseeable damage typical of this type of contract at the time of formation.

(3) Liability for simple negligence is otherwise excluded.

(4) The above limitations also operate in favour of the Contractor’s vicarious agents.

(5) No change in the burden of proof to the Client’s detriment is associated with the above provisions.

Section 14 Data backup

(1) The Client is itself responsible for the regular backup of its data and systems.

(2) Before any intervention by the Contractor in a system in productive use, the Client confirms on request that a current and restorable backup exists.

(3) Paragraphs 1 and 2 leave the Contractor’s liability under Section 13 unaffected; in particular, liability for intent and gross negligence is not limited by them.

Section 15 Confidentiality, use of AI tooling, subcontractors

(1) Each party treats as confidential all confidential information of the other party that becomes known to it in the course of the cooperation and uses it solely for the purposes of this contract. This obligation survives the end of the contract.

(2) At the Client’s request, project communication and confidential documents are transmitted over end-to-end encrypted channels.

(3) The Contractor uses AI-assisted development tooling in performing the services. He undertakes to operate that tooling exclusively with training opt-out and privacy mode enabled, so that the Client’s content does not feed the training of third-party models. The Contractor cannot pass on a contractual zero-retention guarantee from the providers; attention is expressly drawn to this.

(4) The Client may exclude the use of AI-assisted tooling for its project in text form. In that case the Contractor performs without such tooling; any resulting additional effort and change of dates are reflected in the offer or under Section 5.

(5) The Contractor performs the services himself as a matter of principle. The use of subcontractors requires the Client’s prior consent in text form. The Contractor is responsible for the fault of any subcontractor engaged as for his own fault.

Section 16 Data protection

(1) The Contractor processes the Client’s personal data in accordance with the statutory provisions. Details follow from the Contractor’s privacy policy.

(2) Where, in the course of performance, the Contractor obtains access to personal data for which the Client is the controller, the parties conclude a separate data processing agreement under Art. 28 GDPR before the first such access. These Terms do not replace such an agreement.

Section 17 Use as a reference

(1) The Contractor is entitled, after completion of the project, to name the Client as a reference and to describe the services rendered in general terms.

(2) Use of the Client’s logo, screenshots of the work results and publication of specific figures require the Client’s separate consent in text form. At the Client’s request, figures are published in anonymised form only.

(3) The Client may withdraw consent under paragraphs 1 and 2 at any time in text form with effect for the future. Content already published is removed within a reasonable period after receipt of the withdrawal; there is no retroactive obligation.

(4) Where the parties have concluded a confidentiality agreement, that agreement prevails over paragraphs 1 to 3 unless it expressly provides otherwise.

Section 18 Term and termination

(1) Contracts for one-off works services end on acceptance and payment in full.

(2) Continuing obligations, in particular maintenance and support contracts, are concluded for an indefinite period. Either party may terminate them in text form giving one month’s notice to the end of a month. Section 25 applies additionally to consumers.

(3) The right to terminate for good cause remains unaffected.

(4) In the case of works contracts the Client may terminate at any time until completion of the work (§ 648 BGB). In that case the Contractor retains the claim to the agreed remuneration; he must, however, allow to be set off what he saves in expenses as a result of the cancellation or acquires through other use of his labour. It is presumed that he is entitled to five per cent of the remuneration attributable to the part of the service not yet rendered. Both parties remain free to prove a higher or lower amount.

(5) Notices of termination must be given in text form.

Section 19 Force majeure

(1) Events of force majeure that substantially impede or prevent the Contractor’s performance entitle him to postpone performance by the duration of the impediment plus a reasonable restart period. These include in particular official measures, natural disasters, failures of supra-regional communication networks and prolonged disruptions at upstream suppliers, in each case where not attributable to the Contractor.

(2) If the impediment lasts longer than two months, either party may terminate the affected contract. Services already rendered are invoiced.

Section 20 Final provisions

(1) Unless expressly provided otherwise, declarations under this contract must be made in text form. No stricter form than text form is required for declarations by the Client.

(2) The law of the Federal Republic of Germany applies, excluding the UN Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods. As against consumers this applies only to the extent that it does not deprive them of the protection afforded by mandatory provisions of the law of the country in which they have their habitual residence.

(3) The Contractor is neither willing nor obliged to participate in dispute resolution proceedings before a consumer arbitration board (§ 36 VSBG).

(4) Should any provision of these Terms be or become invalid, the validity of the remaining provisions is unaffected. The statutory provisions take the place of the invalid provision.

Part B — Additional provisions applying to consumers

The following provisions apply only where the Client is a consumer within the meaning of § 13 BGB. They prevail over any diverging provision of Part A.

Section 21 Territorial scope of the offer to consumers

(1) The Contractor directs his offer to consumers exclusively at consumers habitually resident in the Federal Republic of Germany.

(2) Contracts with consumers habitually resident outside Germany are formed only where the Contractor expressly confirms this in text form in the individual case.

(3) The offer to businesses is not territorially restricted.

Section 22 Right of withdrawal

(1) Consumers have a statutory right of withdrawal for contracts concluded by distance communication. Details and the model withdrawal form follow from the Contractor’s withdrawal notice, which is attached to the offer.

(2) If the Contractor is to begin performance before the withdrawal period expires, this requires the consumer’s express request. The offer informs the consumer that the right of withdrawal lapses on complete performance and that, on withdrawal after performance has begun, the consumer owes value compensation for the services rendered up to that point (§ 356 Abs. 4, § 357 Abs. 8 BGB).

Section 23 Acceptance as against consumers

The deemed acceptance under Section 7(4) applies to a consumer only where the Contractor has informed the consumer, together with the request for acceptance and in text form, of the consequences of an acceptance that is not declared or is refused without stating defects (§ 640 Abs. 2 Satz 2 BGB). Without that notice the deeming provision does not take effect.

Section 24 Defects and liability as against consumers

(1) The statutory limitation periods for claims in respect of defects are not shortened as against consumers.

(2) No monetary cap on liability applies as against consumers. Section 13 applies unmodified.

(3) No lump sum for default costs is charged to consumers; only costs actually incurred are charged.

Section 25 Term and termination of continuing obligations with consumers

(1) Any initial commitment of the consumer is limited to a maximum of two years.

(2) A tacit extension occurs only for an indefinite period and only on condition that the consumer may terminate the extended contract at any time giving no more than one month’s notice.

(3) The consumer’s notice period is no longer than one month (§ 309 Nr. 9 BGB).

Section 26 Contracts for digital products

(1) Where the Contractor supplies a consumer with a digital product within the meaning of §§ 327 et seq. BGB, the statutory provisions on supply, product defects and updates apply.

(2) The Contractor provides the consumer with the updates necessary to maintain the conformity of the digital product during the relevant period, and informs the consumer of them. This includes security updates (§ 327f BGB).

(3) The Contractor offers the consumer, in the offer, a separate maintenance contract covering the ongoing care and updating of the digital product. Whether the consumer accepts that offer is relevant to determining the relevant period.

(4) If the consumer fails to install an update provided to it within a reasonable period, the Contractor is not liable for a product defect attributable solely to the absence of that update, provided the Contractor had informed the consumer of the availability of the update and of the consequences of not installing it (§ 327f Abs. 2 BGB).

(5) A departure from the objective requirements for the digital product is effective only where the consumer was specifically informed of it before making its contractual declaration and the departure was expressly and separately agreed in the contract (§ 327h BGB). Such a departure is not agreed by these Terms but only in the individual case in the offer.

Part C — Additional provisions applying to businesses

The following provisions apply only where the Client is a business within the meaning of § 14 BGB, a legal person under public law or a special fund under public law. They prevail over any diverging provision of Part A.

Section 27 Limitation of claims in respect of defects

The limitation period for claims in respect of defects is one year from acceptance. This does not apply to claims for damage arising from injury to life, body or health, to claims based on intent or gross negligence, to fraudulent concealment of a defect, or to claims under the Product Liability Act; the statutory periods apply to those.

Section 28 Cap on liability

(1) Within the scope of Section 13(2), the Contractor’s liability for an individual occurrence of loss is limited to the amount of the remuneration agreed for the affected assignment.

(2) The cap under paragraph 1 does not apply to damage arising from injury to life, body or health, to intent and gross negligence, to fraudulent concealment of a defect, to the extent of any guarantee given, or to claims under the Product Liability Act.

Section 29 Set-off and retention

The Client may set off only against claims that are undisputed or have been finally determined by a court. A right of retention is available to the Client only where its counterclaim arises from the same contractual relationship.

Section 30 Late payment

For payment claims against businesses, the Contractor may claim a lump sum of 40 euros in addition to statutory default interest (§ 288 Abs. 5 BGB). The lump sum is to be set off against any damages owed to the extent those comprise costs of legal enforcement.

Section 31 No right of withdrawal; §§ 327 et seq. BGB do not apply

Businesses have no right of withdrawal. The provisions of §§ 327 et seq. BGB on consumer contracts for digital products do not apply.

Section 32 Place of performance and jurisdiction

The place of performance for all services is the Contractor’s place of business. The exclusive place of jurisdiction for all disputes arising from or in connection with the contractual relationship is the Contractor’s place of business, provided the Client is a merchant, a legal person under public law or a special fund under public law (§ 38 ZPO). The Contractor is also entitled to sue at the Client’s general place of jurisdiction.

datenschutz.s3Title: 3. No tracking cookies, no marketing analytics
datenschutz.s3p1: This website does not use tracking cookies and does not embed advertising or social media trackers. No services are used that analyse your behaviour for marketing or profiling. No audience measurement or comparable web analytics is performed.
datenschutz.s4p1: If you contact us by email at {{email}} or via the contact form on the website, we process your name, email address, the service area you select (type of enquiry), and your message solely to handle your enquiry and, where applicable, to prepare a contract (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR). Form data is transmitted server-side through the US-based processor Resend for technical delivery to our mailbox; we do not retain form submissions on our systems beyond what is legally required. Data is not shared with further third parties without a legal basis. Details on Resend are provided under Contact form in the full privacy policy. Direct email communication preferably uses Proton Mail; connections between Proton Mail accounts are end-to-end encrypted.
datenschutz.s5p1: We process personal data only for as long as necessary for the respective purposes or where statutory retention obligations apply. After that, data is erased or anonymised unless legitimate interests require further storage.
datenschutz.s6p1: To the extent provided by the GDPR, you have the right of access, rectification, erasure, restriction of processing, objection to processing, and data portability. You also have the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority.
datenschutz.htmlBody:
Privacy Policy

1. An overview of data protection

General information

The following information will provide you with an easy to navigate overview of what will happen with your personal data when you visit this website. The term “personal data” comprises all data that can be used to personally identify you. For detailed information about the subject matter of data protection, please consult our Data Protection Declaration, which we have included beneath this copy.

Data recording on this website

Who is the responsible party for the recording of data on this website (i.e., the “controller”)?

The data on this website is processed by the operator of the website, whose contact information is available under section “Information about the responsible party (referred to as the “controller” in the GDPR)” in this Privacy Policy.

How do we record your data?

We collect your data as a result of your sharing of your data with us. This may, for instance be information you enter into our contact form.

Other data shall be recorded by our IT systems automatically or after you consent to its recording during your website visit. This data comprises primarily technical information (e.g., web browser, operating system, or time the site was accessed). This information is recorded automatically when you access this website.

What are the purposes we use your data for?

A portion of the information is generated to guarantee the error free provision of the website. Other data may be used to analyze your user patterns. If contracts can be concluded or initiated via the website, the transmitted data will also be processed for contract offers, orders or other order enquiries.

What rights do you have as far as your information is concerned?

You have the right to receive information about the source, recipients, and purposes of your archived personal data at any time without having to pay a fee for such disclosures. You also have the right to demand that your data are rectified or eradicated. If you have consented to data processing, you have the option to revoke this consent at any time, which shall affect all future data processing. Moreover, you have the right to demand that the processing of your data be restricted under certain circumstances. Furthermore, you have the right to log a complaint with the competent supervising agency.

Please do not hesitate to contact us at any time if you have questions about this or any other data protection related issues.

2. Hosting

We are hosting the content of our website at the following provider:

External Hosting

This website is hosted externally. Personal data collected on this website are stored on the servers of the host. These may include, but are not limited to, IP addresses, contact requests, metadata and communications, contract information, contact information, names, web page access, and other data generated through a web site.

The external hosting serves the purpose of fulfilling the contract with our potential and existing customers (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR) and in the interest of secure, fast, and efficient provision of our online services by a professional provider (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR). If appropriate consent has been obtained, the processing is carried out exclusively on the basis of Art. 6 (1)(a) GDPR and § 25 (1) TDDDG, insofar the consent includes the storage of cookies or the access to information in the user's end device (e.g., device fingerprinting) within the meaning of the TDDDG. This consent can be revoked at any time.

Our host(s) will only process your data to the extent necessary to fulfil its performance obligations and to follow our instructions with respect to such data.

We are using the following host(s):

Hosting provider

Unternehmen: Vercel Inc.
Adresse: 440 N Barranca Avenue #4133, Covina, CA 91723, USA
Land: Vereinigte Staaten von Amerika (USA)
Website: https://vercel.com
Rechtsform: US-Unternehmen (Delaware Corporation)

Kontakt (Datenschutz / DPA)

E-Mail (Privacy): privacy@vercel.com
Privacy Request Center: https://datarequest.vercel.com/privacy

Dokumente (Datenschutz / AV-Vertrag)

Datenschutzerklärung (Privacy Policy): https://vercel.com/legal/privacy-policy
Auftragsverarbeitungsvertrag (DPA): https://vercel.com/legal/dpa
Rechtliche Hinweise (Legal): https://vercel.com/legal

Data processing

We have concluded a data processing agreement (DPA) for the use of the above-mentioned service. This is a contract mandated by data privacy laws that guarantees that they process personal data of our website visitors only based on our instructions and in compliance with the GDPR.

Data transfer to the USA

Our hosting provider Vercel Inc. is based in the USA, so personal data is transferred there. The transfer is based on the European Commission’s adequacy decision of 10 July 2023 on the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework (Art. 45(1) GDPR): Vercel Inc. is certified under the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework for the “Non-HR Data” category and has thereby undertaken to comply with European data protection standards. The certification can be inspected in the official list maintained by the U.S. Department of Commerce: https://www.dataprivacyframework.gov/list

3. General information and mandatory information

Data protection

The operators of this website and its pages take the protection of your personal data very seriously. Hence, we handle your personal data as confidential information and in compliance with the statutory data protection regulations and this Data Protection Declaration.

Whenever you use this website, a variety of personal information will be collected. Personal data comprises data that can be used to personally identify you. This Data Protection Declaration explains which data we collect as well as the purposes we use this data for. It also explains how, and for which purpose the information is collected.

We herewith advise you that the transmission of data via the Internet (i.e., through e-mail communications) may be prone to security gaps. It is not possible to completely protect data against third-party access.

Information about the responsible party (referred to as the “controller” in the GDPR)

The data processing controller on this website is:

Danijel Kresic
Burggasse 3
89604 Allmendingen

E-mail: kresic.systems@protonmail.com

The controller is the natural person or legal entity that single-handedly or jointly with others makes decisions as to the purposes of and resources for the processing of personal data (e.g., names, e-mail addresses, etc.).

Storage duration

Unless a more specific storage period has been specified in this privacy policy, your personal data will remain with us until the purpose for which it was collected no longer applies. If you assert a justified request for deletion or revoke your consent to data processing, your data will be deleted, unless we have other legally permissible reasons for storing your personal data (e.g., tax or commercial law retention periods); in the latter case, the deletion will take place after these reasons cease to apply.

General information on the legal basis for the data processing on this website

If you have consented to data processing, we process your personal data on the basis of Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR or Art. 9 (2)(a) GDPR, if special categories of data are processed according to Art. 9 (1) DSGVO. In the case of explicit consent to the transfer of personal data to third countries, the data processing is also based on Art. 49 (1)(a) GDPR. If you have consented to the storage of cookies or to the access to information in your end device (e.g., via device fingerprinting), the data processing is additionally based on § 25 (1) TDDDG. The consent can be revoked at any time. If your data is required for the fulfillment of a contract or for the implementation of pre-contractual measures, we process your data on the basis of Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR. Furthermore, if your data is required for the fulfillment of a legal obligation, we process it on the basis of Art. 6(1)(c) GDPR. Furthermore, the data processing may be carried out on the basis of our legitimate interest according to Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR. Information on the relevant legal basis in each individual case is provided in the following paragraphs of this privacy policy.

Recipients of personal data

In the scope of our business activities, we cooperate with various external parties. In some cases, this also requires the transfer of personal data to these external parties. We only disclose personal data to external parties if this is required as part of the fulfillment of a contract, if we are legally obligated to do so (e.g., disclosure of data to tax authorities), if we have a legitimate interest in the disclosure pursuant to Art. 6 (1)(f) GDPR, or if another legal basis permits the disclosure of this data. When using processors, we only disclose personal data of our customers on the basis of a valid contract on data processing. In the case of joint processing, a joint processing agreement is concluded.

Revocation of your consent to the processing of data

A wide range of data processing transactions are possible only subject to your express consent. You can also revoke at any time any consent you have already given us. This shall be without prejudice to the lawfulness of any data collection that occurred prior to your revocation.

Right to object to the collection of data in special cases; right to object to direct advertising (Art. 21 GDPR)

IN THE EVENT THAT DATA ARE PROCESSED ON THE BASIS OF ART. 6(1)(E) OR (F) GDPR, YOU HAVE THE RIGHT TO AT ANY TIME OBJECT TO THE PROCESSING OF YOUR PERSONAL DATA BASED ON GROUNDS ARISING FROM YOUR UNIQUE SITUATION. THIS ALSO APPLIES TO ANY PROFILING BASED ON THESE PROVISIONS. TO DETERMINE THE LEGAL BASIS, ON WHICH ANY PROCESSING OF DATA IS BASED, PLEASE CONSULT THIS DATA PROTECTION DECLARATION. IF YOU LOG AN OBJECTION, WE WILL NO LONGER PROCESS YOUR AFFECTED PERSONAL DATA, UNLESS WE ARE IN A POSITION TO PRESENT COMPELLING PROTECTION WORTHY GROUNDS FOR THE PROCESSING OF YOUR DATA, THAT OUTWEIGH YOUR INTERESTS, RIGHTS AND FREEDOMS OR IF THE PURPOSE OF THE PROCESSING IS THE CLAIMING, EXERCISING OR DEFENCE OF LEGAL ENTITLEMENTS (OBJECTION PURSUANT TO ART. 21(1) GDPR).

IF YOUR PERSONAL DATA IS BEING PROCESSED IN ORDER TO ENGAGE IN DIRECT ADVERTISING, YOU HAVE THE RIGHT TO OBJECT TO THE PROCESSING OF YOUR AFFECTED PERSONAL DATA FOR THE PURPOSES OF SUCH ADVERTISING AT ANY TIME. THIS ALSO APPLIES TO PROFILING TO THE EXTENT THAT IT IS AFFILIATED WITH SUCH DIRECT ADVERTISING. IF YOU OBJECT, YOUR PERSONAL DATA WILL SUBSEQUENTLY NO LONGER BE USED FOR DIRECT ADVERTISING PURPOSES (OBJECTION PURSUANT TO ART. 21(2) GDPR).

Right to log a complaint with the competent supervisory agency

In the event of violations of the GDPR, data subjects are entitled to log a complaint with a supervisory agency, in particular in the member state where they usually maintain their domicile, place of work or at the place where the alleged violation occurred. The right to log a complaint is in effect regardless of any other administrative or court proceedings available as legal recourses.

Right to data portability

You have the right to have data that we process automatically on the basis of your consent or in fulfillment of a contract handed over to you or to a third party in a common, machine-readable format. If you should demand the direct transfer of the data to another controller, this will be done only if it is technically feasible.

Information about, rectification and eradication of data

Within the scope of the applicable statutory provisions, you have the right to demand information about your archived personal data, their source and recipients as well as the purpose of the processing of your data at any time. You may also have a right to have your data rectified or eradicated. If you have questions about this subject matter or any other questions about personal data, please do not hesitate to contact us at any time.

Right to demand processing restrictions

You have the right to demand the imposition of restrictions as far as the processing of your personal data is concerned. To do so, you may contact us at any time. The right to demand restriction of processing applies in the following cases:

  • In the event that you should dispute the correctness of your data archived by us, we will usually need some time to verify this claim. During the time that this investigation is ongoing, you have the right to demand that we restrict the processing of your personal data.
  • If the processing of your personal data was/is conducted in an unlawful manner, you have the option to demand the restriction of the processing of your data instead of demanding the eradication of this data.
  • If we do not need your personal data any longer and you need it to exercise, defend or claim legal entitlements, you have the right to demand the restriction of the processing of your personal data instead of its eradication.
  • If you have raised an objection pursuant to Art. 21(1) GDPR, your rights and our rights will have to be weighed against each other. As long as it has not been determined whose interests prevail, you have the right to demand a restriction of the processing of your personal data.

If you have restricted the processing of your personal data, these data – with the exception of their archiving – may be processed only subject to your consent or to claim, exercise or defend legal entitlements or to protect the rights of other natural persons or legal entities or for important public interest reasons cited by the European Union or a member state of the EU.

SSL and/or TLS encryption

For security reasons and to protect the transmission of confidential content, such as purchase orders or inquiries you submit to us as the website operator, this website uses either an SSL or a TLS encryption program. You can recognize an encrypted connection by checking whether the address line of the browser switches from “http://” to “https://” and also by the appearance of the lock icon in the browser line.

If the SSL or TLS encryption is activated, data you transmit to us cannot be read by third parties.

4. Recording of data on this website

Cookies

This website uses a single cookie. There is no tracking, no audience measurement and no integration of advertising networks.

  • NEXT_LOCALE – stores the language you selected via the language switcher (value: de or en) so that opening the home page presents it to you in that language. Lifetime: 12 months. Attributes: SameSite=Lax and, over HTTPS connections, Secure. The cookie is only set once you actively switch the language and contains no personal data.

This cookie is stored without consent pursuant to Section 25(2)(2) TDDDG, because it is strictly necessary in order to provide the service you have expressly requested – displaying this website in the language you selected. Insofar as personal data are processed in this context, the processing is based on our legitimate interest in the error-free and user-friendly presentation of this website (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).

You may delete cookies in your browser at any time or prevent their storage altogether. The website remains fully usable in that case; the language selection is simply not retained beyond the visit.

Server log files

The provider of this website and its pages automatically collects and stores information in so-called server log files, which your browser communicates to us automatically. The information comprises:

  • The type and version of browser used
  • The used operating system
  • Referrer URL
  • The hostname of the accessing computer
  • The time of the server inquiry
  • The IP address

This data is not merged with other data sources.

This data is recorded on the basis of Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR. The operator of the website has a legitimate interest in the technically error free depiction and the optimization of the operator’s website. In order to achieve this, server log files must be recorded.

Contact form

If you submit inquiries via our contact form, we store the information entered in the form, including the contact details you provide and the service area you select (for example web architecture, WebGL, or AI automation), in order to process your enquiry and in case we need follow-up questions. Recording the service area allows us to assign your enquiry to the appropriate category and respond in a targeted manner. We will not disclose this data without your consent.

When the form is submitted, your IP address is processed briefly in memory to prevent abusive bulk submissions. It is not stored permanently and is discarded after one minute at the latest. The legal basis is our legitimate interest in protection against misuse (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).

Email delivery via Resend

To send messages from our contact form by email, we use Resend (2261 Market Street #5039, San Francisco, CA 94114, USA). Resend provides the technical infrastructure for email delivery. The data you enter in the form is transmitted to Resend’s servers and processed there to deliver the message to our inbox.

This processing is based on Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR (legitimate interests in fast and reliable handling of correspondence). We have concluded a data processing agreement (DPA) with Resend. Further information is available in Resend’s privacy policy: https://resend.com/legal/privacy-policy.

Resend likewise processes the data in the USA. That transfer is also based on the adequacy decision on the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework (Art. 45(1) GDPR); the provider is certified there for the “Non-HR Data” category (https://www.dataprivacyframework.gov/list).

The processing of these data is based on Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR, if your request is related to the execution of a contract or if it is necessary to carry out pre-contractual measures. In all other cases the processing is based on our legitimate interest in the effective processing of the requests addressed to us (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR) or on your agreement (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR) if this has been requested; the consent can be revoked at any time.

The information you have entered into the contact form shall remain with us until you ask us to eradicate the data, revoke your consent to the archiving of data or if the purpose for which the information is being archived no longer exists (e.g., after we have concluded our response to your inquiry). This shall be without prejudice to any mandatory legal provisions, in particular retention periods.

Request by e-mail

If you contact us by e-mail, your request, including all resulting personal data (name, request) will be stored and processed by us for the purpose of processing your request. We do not pass these data on without your consent.

These data are processed on the basis of Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR if your inquiry is related to the fulfillment of a contract or is required for the performance of pre-contractual measures. In all other cases, the data are processed on the basis of our legitimate interest in the effective handling of inquiries submitted to us (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR) or on the basis of your consent (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR) if it has been obtained; the consent can be revoked at any time.

The data sent by you to us via contact requests remain with us until you request us to delete, revoke your consent to the storage or the purpose for the data storage lapses (e.g. after completion of your request). Mandatory statutory provisions - in particular statutory retention periods - remain unaffected.
